title: Professional muzokaralar
goal_uz: Dars oxirida ingliz tilida murakkab muzokaralarni olib borasiz: tayyorgarlik va BATNA tilini, framing va anchoring texnikalarini, yumshatish va hedging iboralarini hamda pozitsiya to‘xtab qolgan holatlarda muzokarani davom etteasiz.

vocab.uz: kelishuvga kelmgan taqdirdagi eng yaxshi alternativ (best alternative to a negotiated agreement)
langar (muzokarada birinchi taklif sifatida berilgan raqam)
to‘xtab qolgan holat (ikki tomon ham siljimaydi)
ramkalash (masala qaysi tomondan ko‘rib chiqilishini belgilash)

scenes.title: Bugun: professional muzokaralar
board: Professional Negotiation
Preparation · BATNA · Framing · Anchoring · Hedging · Deadlock

examples.t: If you can do Friday, we could stretch the budget.
examples.uz: Agar juma kuni qila olsangiz, byudjetni cho‘zishimiz mumkin.

scenes.say_native: Assalomu alaykum! PRO 1 kursimizning yakuniy loyihasi va imtihonini tugatgach, PRO 2 — C1 darajasiga o‘tamiz. Bugun birinchi mavzu — professional muzokaralar. Murakkab muzokaralar ingliz tilida qanday olib boriladi: tayyorgarlik, BATNA, framing, anchoring, hedging va deadlock holatlarida harakat. Bu ko‘nikmalar ish intervyulari, mijozlar bilan muzokaralar va IELTS nutqining har ob-havosida kerak. Boshlaymiz. Murakkab muzokara quyidagicha ishlaydi: har bir tomonning ochiq raqami ortida yashirin qiziqishi bor — siz esa faqat raqamni emas, qiziqishni o‘qishingiz kerak.
scenes.say: Welcome to PRO 2 — C1. Today we start with professional negotiation: preparation and BATNA language, framing and anchoring, hedging and softening, and what to do when talks deadlock. These skills matter in job interviews, client negotiations and even IELTS speaking at the highest level. Let's begin.
scenes.say_uz: PRO 2 — C1 darajasiga xush kelibsiz! Bugun birinchi mavzu — professional muzokaralar: tayyorgarlik va BATNA tili, framing va anchoring, hedging va deadlock holatlari. Bu ko‘nikmalar ish intervyulari, mijoz muzokaralari va IELTS nutqining yuqori darajasida kerak. Boshlaymiz.

scenes.title: Muzokaraga tayyorgarlik
board: Know your BATNA before you walk in
Set: aspiration price · resistance point · opening offer
Know the other side: priorities, pressures, deadlines
scenes.say_native: Tayyorgarlik: muzokaraga eshikdan kirishdan oldin BATNA — kelishuvga kelmagan taqdirdagi eng yaxshi alternativangizni biling. Uchta nuqtasini belgilang: aspiration — umid qiligan eng yaxshi natija; resistance point — undan ortiq yon bermaydigan chegarangiz; opening offer — birinchi taklifingiz. Raqib tomonni ham biling: ustuvorliklari, bosimlari, muddatlari. Ingliz tilidagi muzokara aynan shundan boshlanadi. Raqib tomonning muddatini bilsangiz, strategiyangiz avtomatik ravishda to‘g‘rilanadi — vaqti kam bo‘lgan tomon ko‘proq yon beradi.
scenes.say: Preparation. Before you walk in, know your BATNA — the best alternative if no deal is reached. Set three points: your aspiration — the best you hope for; your resistance point — where you walk away; and your opening offer. Know the other side too: their priorities, pressures and deadlines. English negotiation always starts here.
scenes.say_uz: Tayyorgarlik. Eshikdan kirishdan oldin BATNA — kelishuvga kelmagan taqdirdagi eng yaxshi alternativangizni biling. Uchta nuqta belgilang: umid qilingan eng yaxshi natija, yon bermaydigan chegarangiz va birinchi taklifingiz. Raqib tomonni ham biling — ustuvorliklari, bosimi, muddatlari. Inglizcha muzokara aynan shundan boshlanadi.

scenes.title: BATNA tili
board: “If we can't agree, our alternative is …”
“We're prepared to explore other options.”
“Walking away is not our preference, but …”

examples.t: If we can't reach agreement, our plan B is to work with a local supplier.
examples.uz: Agar kelisha olmasak, B rejamiz — mahalliy yetkazib beruvchi bilan ishlash.

scenes.say_native: BATNA tilining ingliz iboralari: “If we can't agree, our alternative is…” — agar kelisha olmasak, alternativamiz…; “We're prepared to explore other options.” — boshqa variantlarni ko‘rib chiqishga tayyormiz; “Walking away is not our preference, but…” — undan voz kechishni xohlamaymiz, ammo… Bu gaplar sizga shartnoma tuzmaslik huquqini eslatib turadi — muzokarada eng kuchli qurol. BATNA sizga jim turishni o‘rgatadi: “Yo‘q” deya olish kuchsizlarni ham kuchli ko‘rsatadi — chunki tanlovingiz borligini biladi.
scenes.say: BATNA language: “If we can't agree, our alternative is…”; “We're prepared to explore other options.”; “Walking away is not our preference, but…” These sentences remind everyone in the room that you don't have to sign — the strongest quiet weapon in any negotiation.
scenes.say_uz: BATNA tili: “If we can't agree, our alternative is…” — kelisha olmasak, alternativamiz…; “We're prepared to explore other options.” — boshqa variantlarni ko‘rib chiqishga tayyormiz; “Walking away is not our preference, but…” — rad qilishni xohlamaymiz, ammo… Bu gaplar xonadagilarga siz imzo qo‘ymasligingiz mumkinligini eslatadi — eng kuchli tinch qurol.

scenes.title: BATNA iboralarini baland ayting
board: Your counterpart pushes a low price.
State your BATNA, aloud, three ways
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Qarshi tomon past narx qo‘ymoqda. Ovoz chiqarib BATNA iboralarini uch xil ayting — ingliz tilida. Sekin va tiniq gapiring, ovozda bosimsiz ishonch bo‘lsin.
scenes.say: Your counterpart pushes a low price. State your BATNA aloud three different ways. Speak slowly and clearly, with calm confidence — no pressure in your voice.
scenes.say_uz: Qarshi tomon past narx qo‘ymoqda. BATNA iboralarini ovoz chiqarib uch xil ayting — ingliz tilida. Sekin, tiniq va bosimsiz, ishonch bilan gapiring.

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: “If we can't agree, our alternative is to…”
“We're prepared to explore other options.”
“Walking away is not our preference, but…”
scenes.say_native: Javoblar: uchala ibora ham to‘g‘ri. Endi muzokaradagi birinchi strategiyaga o‘tamiz — framing va anchoring.
scenes.say: Answers: all three work. Now the first strategy inside the room — framing and anchoring.
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar: uchalasi ham to‘g‘ri. Endi xonadagi birinchi strategiya — framing va anchoring.

scenes.title: Anchoring: birinchi raqamni ayting
board: First number anchors the whole negotiation
Aim slightly beyond your aspiration
“We were thinking in the region of £48,000.”

examples.t: We were thinking in the region of £48,000.
examples.uz: Biz qirq sakkiz ming funt atrofida o‘ylayapmiz.

scenes.say_native: Anchoring: birinchi aytilgan raqam butun muzokarani o‘ziga tortadi. O‘z aspiratingizdan biroz yuqoriroq raqam qo‘ying — bo‘sh joy qoldiring. Ingliz tilida: “We were thinking in the region of…” — biz… atrofida o‘ylayapmiz; “Around…” — taxminan; “Ballpark figure:…” — taxminiy raqam. Agar raqib birinchi qo‘ysa, uni eslang, lekin anglam bilan boshlang — “That's higher than we can do” deb rad etmang, avval so‘rang. Raqamni aytganingizda pauza qiling va kuting — jimlik raqibni gapirishga majbur qiladi, ko‘pincha u o‘zi pasayadi.
scenes.say: Anchoring. The first number said out loud pulls the whole negotiation toward it. Set yours slightly above your aspiration — leave room to move. In English: “We were thinking in the region of…” or “Around…” or “Ballpark figure:…” If the counterpart anchors first, acknowledge it but don't reject it outright — ask questions before you react.
scenes.say_uz: Anchoring. Birinchi aytilgan raqam butun muzokarani o‘ziga tortadi. O‘z umidingizdan biroz yuqoriroq qo‘ying — joy qoldiring. Inglizcha: “We were thinking in the region of…” —…atrofida; “Around…” — taxminan; “Ballpark figure:…” — taxminiy raqam. Agar raqib birinchi qo‘ysa, rad etmang — avval so‘rang, keyin reaksiya bildiring.

scenes.title: Anchoring iboralarini ayting
board: Open at £52,000 for a project worth £48,000.
Say the anchor three ways, aloud
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Qiymati qirq sakkiz ming funtlik loyihaga ellik ikki mingdan boshlang. Uch xil ayting: “We were thinking in the region of…”, “Around…”, “Ballpark figure…”. Ovoz chiqarib, klubda muloyim talaffuz qiling.
scenes.say: Open negotiations at fifty-two thousand pounds for a project worth forty-eight. Say the anchor three ways: “We were thinking in the region of…”, “Around…”, “Ballpark figure…” — aloud.
scenes.say_uz: Qiymati qirq sakkiz ming funtlik loyihaga ellik ikkidan boshlang. Anchorni uch xil ayting: “We were thinking in the region of…”, “Around…”, “Ballpark figure…” Baland ovozda.

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: “We were thinking in the region of £52,000.”
“Ballpark figure: £52,000.”
scenes.say_native: Javoblar: uchala ibora langar qo‘yadi. Endi framing — masalani qaysi tomondan ko‘rsatishni o‘rganamiz.
scenes.say: Answers: all three set the anchor. Now framing — choosing which side of the table the issue is viewed from.
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar: uchalasi ham langar qo‘yadi. Endi framing — masalani qaysi tomondan ko‘rsatish.

scenes.title: Framing: yutish yoki yo‘qotish
board: Gain frame: “This saves you £10,000 a year.”
Loss frame: “Without this, you lose £10,000 a year.”
Both true — different weight

examples.t: This saves your team thirty hours a month.
examples.uz: Bu jamoangizga oyiga o‘ttiz soat tejash beradi.

scenes.say_native: Framing: bir xil dalilni ikki xil ko‘rsatish mumkin. Yutish ramkasi — “This saves you…” — bu sizga … tejaydi. Yo‘qotish ramkasi — “Without this, you lose…” — busiz … yo‘qotasiz. Yo‘qotish ramkasiga odamlar ko‘proq ta’sirchan — psixologik jihatdan yo‘qotish og‘riqliroq. Ammo mijoz bilan munosabatda yutish ramkasini ishlating — o‘zingizni bosimga solmang. Endi mashq qilamiz. Yutish yoki yo‘qotish ramkasini tanlashni mijozning temperamentiga qarab qiling: tavakkal qiladigan mijozga yo‘qotish ramkasini, ehtiyotkor mijozga yutish ramkasini bering.
scenes.say: Framing. The same fact can be shown two ways. The gain frame: “This saves you…” — you gain by acting. The loss frame: “Without this, you lose…” — you lose by not acting. People feel loss more strongly than gain, but with long-term clients, prefer the gain frame — nobody signs under pressure happily. Now practice.
scenes.say_uz: Framing. Bir xil dalilni ikki xil ko‘rsatish mumkin. Yutish ramkasi: “This saves you…” — harakat qilib yutasiz. Yo‘qotish ramkasi: “Without this, you lose…” — harakat qilmasangiz yo‘qotasiz. Yo‘qotish og‘riqlisi — shuni yodda tuting. Ammo uzun muddatli mijozlar bilan yutish ramkasini ishlating. Endi mashq.

scenes.title: Framing mashqi
board: Claim: your software saves 30 hours a month.
Say it as a gain frame, then a loss frame — aloud
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Da’vo: dasturingiz oyiga o‘ttiz soat tejaydi. Avval yutish ramkasi: “This saves your team thirty hours a month.” — baland ovozda. Keyin yo‘qotish: “Without this, every month your team loses thirty hours.” — baland ovozda. Ikkalasini ohang bilan ayting.
scenes.say: Claim: your software saves thirty hours a month. Say it as a gain frame — “This saves your team thirty hours a month.” Then as a loss frame — “Without this, you lose thirty hours every month.” Aloud, with feeling.
scenes.say_uz: Da’vo: dasturingiz oyiga o‘ttiz soat tejaydi. Yutish ramkasi bilan ayting: “This saves your team thirty hours a month.” Keyin yo‘qotish ramkasi: “Without this, you lose thirty hours every month.” Ohang bilan baland ovozda.

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: Gain: “This saves your team thirty hours a month.”
Loss: “Without this, you lose thirty hours every month.”
scenes.say_native: Javoblar: yutish — “This saves your team thirty hours a month.”; yo‘qotish — “Without this, you lose thirty hours every month.” Endi yumshatish — hedging tilini o‘rganamiz.
scenes.say: Answers: the gain frame and the loss frame. Now the language of hedging — how to soften every demand.
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar: yutish ramkasi va yo‘qotish ramkasi. Endi hedging — har bir talabni yumshatish tili.

scenes.title: Hedging va yumshatish
board: “Perhaps…” “Might…” “I wonder if…”
“Would it be possible…?” “I was hoping…”
“A little more flexible on…” “Around…”

examples.t: Would it be possible to revisit the payment terms?
examples.uz: To‘lov shartlarini qayta ko‘rib chiqish mumkinmi?

scenes.say_native: Hedging — talabni yumshoq qilish: “Perhaps…” — ehtimol; “Might…” — mumkinmi; “I wonder if…” — qiziquv; “Would it be possible…?” — mumkinmi?; “I was hoping…” — umid qilgandim; “A little more flexible on…” — biroz moslashuvchan bo‘ling; “Around…” — taxminan. West’larda muzokara haqiqatan muzokaradir — chunki hech narsa qat’iy emas. Endi mashq qilamiz. Britaniyaliklar “Perhaps we could…” deb boshlaydi va baribir maqsadiga erishadi — yumshoqlik zaiflik emas, madaniyat.
scenes.say: Hedging — softening every demand. “Perhaps…”, “Might…”, “I wonder if…”, “Would it be possible…?”, “I was hoping…”, “A little more flexible on…”, “Around…” — British negotiation works because nothing is presented as absolutely fixed. Now practice.
scenes.say_uz: Hedging — talabni yumshatish: “Perhaps…” — ehtimol; “Might…” — mumkinmi; “I wonder if…” — qiziq; “Would it be possible…?” — mumkinmi; “I was hoping…” — umid qilgandim; “A little more flexible on…” — moslashuvchan bo‘ling; “Around…” — taxminan. Britaniya muzokarasi shuni talab qiladi — hech narsani qat’iy aytmang. Endi mashq.

scenes.title: Talabni yumshating
board: ✗ “Lower the price.”
✓ “I was hoping we could be a little more flexible on price.”
Soften three demands, aloud
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Uchta tajovuzkor talabni yumshating: “Lower the price.” — narxni tushiring; “Change the deadline.” — muddatni o‘zgartiring; “Send the samples today.” — namunalarni bugun yuboring. Har birini “I was hoping…” yoki “Would it be possible…?” bilan yumshatib baland ayting.
scenes.say: Soften three blunt demands aloud: “Lower the price.” “Change the deadline.” “Send the samples today.” Turn each into “I was hoping…” or “Would it be possible…?”
scenes.say_uz: Uchta to‘g‘ridan-to‘g‘ri talabni yumshating: “Lower the price.” “Change the deadline.” “Send the samples today.” Har birini “I was hoping…” yoki “Would it be possible…?” ga aylantirib baland ayting.

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: “I was hoping we could be a little more flexible on price.”
“Would it be possible to revisit the deadline?”
“I wonder if the samples could ship today.”
scenes.say_native: Javoblar: “I was hoping we could be a little more flexible on price.” — narxni biroz moslashishimiz mumkinmi?; “Would it be possible to revisit the deadline?” — muddatni qayta ko‘rib chiqish mumkinmi?; “I wonder if the samples could ship today.” — namunalar bugun jo‘nashi mumkinmi? Endi murosaga kelish — concession tilini o‘rganamiz.
scenes.say: Answers: “I was hoping we could be a little more flexible on price,” “Would it be possible to revisit the deadline,” and “I wonder if the samples could ship today.” Now the language of concessions — trading, never giving.
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar: “I was hoping we could be a little more flexible on price.” “Would it be possible to revisit the deadline?” “I wonder if the samples could ship today.” Endi concession tili — yon berish, lekin bermasdan so‘rash.

scenes.title: Concession: bermang, almashing
board: “If you …, we could …”
“We'd need something in return.”
“On that condition, we could …”

examples.t: If you commit to two years, we could reduce the rate.
examples.uz: Agar ikki yilga majburiy bo‘lsangiz, stavkani tushirishimiz mumkin.

scenes.say_native: Concession: hech qachon yon bermang — almashing. Ingliz tilida qoliplar: “If you…, we could…” — agar … qilsangiz, biz … qilishimiz mumkin; “We'd need something in return.” — evaziga nimadir olishimiz kerak; “On that condition, we could…” — o‘sha shart asosida biz … Endi hech narsani shartsiz bermaysiz. Endi mashq qilamiz. Almashishda “something in return” iborasini qo‘yganingizda hech kim sizni ochko‘z deb o‘ylamaydi — bu professional etika.
scenes.say: Concessions — trade, never give. The frames: “If you…, we could…”; “We'd need something in return.”; “On that condition, we could…” From now on, no concession leaves the table without something coming back. Now practice.
scenes.say_uz: Concessions — bermang, almashing. Qoliplar: “If you…, we could…” — agar … bo‘lsa, biz …; “We'd need something in return.” — evaziga nimadir kerak; “On that condition, we could…” — o‘sha shartda. Bundan buyon hech qanday yon berish evazsiz ketmaydi. Endi mashq.

scenes.title: Almashish iboralarini tuzing
board: They want: 10% discount.
You want: longer contract + faster payment.
Make two offers, aloud
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Qarshi tomon chisq foiz chegirma xohlaydi. Siz esa uzunroq shartnoma va tezroq to‘lovni xohlaysiz. Ikki almashish taklifi tuzing: “If you…, we could…” bilan. Baland ovozda ayting.
scenes.say: Your counterpart wants a ten percent discount. You want a longer contract and faster payment. Make two trade offers aloud, using “If you…, we could…”
scenes.say_uz: Qarshi tomon o‘n foiz chegirma xohlaydi. Siz uzunroq shartnoma va tezroq to‘lovni xohlaysiz. “If you…, we could…” bilan ikki taklif tuzing — baland ovozda.

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: “If you sign a two-year contract, we could offer ten percent.”
“If you pay within thirty days, we could make it work.”
scenes.say_native: Javoblar: “If you sign a two-year contract, we could offer ten percent.” — agar ikki yillik shartnomaga imzo chekayotgan bo‘lsangiz, o‘n foiz berishimiz mumkin. “If you pay within thirty days, we could make it work.” — o‘ttiz kun ichida to‘lasangiz, bu ishlashi mumkin. Hech qachon evazsiz bermang. Endi deadlock — to‘xtab qolgan holatlarni o‘rganamiz.
scenes.say: Answers: “If you sign a two-year contract, we could offer ten percent,” and “If you pay within thirty days, we could make it work.” Never give without a return. Now deadlock — when talks freeze.
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar: “If you sign a two-year contract, we could offer ten percent.” Va “If you pay within thirty days, we could make it work.” Hech qachon evazsiz bermang. Endi deadlock — muzokara to‘xtab qolsa.

scenes.title: Deadlock bo‘lsa qo‘llanadigan til
board: “Let me think about that.”
“Could we park that and come back to it?”
“What would it take to reach agreement today?”
“Let's split the difference.”

examples.t: Could we park that and come back after lunch?
examples.uz: Buni tushlikdan keyin qoldirib, keyin qaytishimiz mumkinmi?

scenes.say_native: Deadlock — ikki tomon ham siljimasa. Ingliz tilida chiqish yo‘llari: “Let me think about that.” — buni o‘ylab ko‘ray; “Could we park that and come back to it?” — buni keyinga qoldirib, keyin qaytishimiz mumkinmi; “What would it take to reach agreement today?” — bugun kelishish uchun nima kerak; “Let's split the difference.” — o‘rtani topamiz; “Take a break and…” — tanaffus olib… Hozir xonadagi haroratni pastga tushirish kerak — hech qachon g‘azab bilan yechim topmaysiz. Endi mashq qilamiz. Tanaffus olishning kuchi: besh daqiqalik jimlik yigirmaga xato qarordan saqlab qoladi — muzokarada shoshilish dushman.
scenes.say: Deadlock — when both sides stop moving. Ways through in English: “Let me think about that.” “Could we park that and come back to it?” “What would it take to reach agreement today?” “Let's split the difference.” “Take a break and…” The priority is lowering the temperature in the room — you never solve a deadlock angry. Now practice.
scenes.say_uz: Deadlock — ikki tomon ham siljimasa. Chiqish yo‘llari: “Let me think about that.” — buni o‘ylab ko‘ray; “Could we park that and come back to it?” — buni keyinga qoldiraylik; “What would it take to reach agreement today?” — bugun kelishish uchun nima kerak; “Let's split the difference.” — o‘rtani topamiz; “Take a break and…” — tanaffus olib… Eng muhimi — xonadagi haroratni tushirish. Hech qachon g‘azab bilan yechim topmaysiz. Endi mashq.

scenes.title: Deadlock yechimlari
board: The other side won't move on price.
Say three deadlock phrases, aloud
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Qarshi tomon narxdan siljimayapti. Uchta deadlock iborasini baland ovozda ayting — tiniq va muloyim ohangda.
scenes.say: Your counterpart won't move on price. Say three deadlock phrases aloud — clear and calm, never raised.
scenes.say_uz: Qarshi tomon narxdan siljimayapti. Deadlock iboralaridan uchtasini baland ovozda ayting — tiniq va muloyim ovozda.

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: “Let me think about that.”
“Could we park that and come back to it?”
“What would it take to reach agreement today?”
scenes.say_native: Javoblar: uchala ibora ham to‘g‘ri. Endi butun jarayonni — tayyorgarlikdan yopilishgacha — tinglash orqali ko‘ramiz.
scenes.say: Answers: all three work. Now the whole process — preparation to close — in one listening.
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar: uchalasi ham to‘g‘ri. Endi butun jarayonni — tayyorgarlikdan yopilishgacha — tinglov orqali ko‘ramiz.

scenes.title: Tinglash: to‘liq muzokara
board: Listen: supplier and buyer — 3 rounds
Then three questions
scenes.say_native: Endi to‘liq muzokarani tinglang — yetkazib beruvchi va xaridor o‘rtasida, uch raund. BATNA, framing, hedging va deadlock iboralarini tutib qolishga harakat qiling. Uch savol keladi. Tinglang: uch raundda anchor, trade va deadlock ketma-ketligini his qiling — real uchrashuvlarda ham shunchaki.
scenes.say: Now listen to a full negotiation — a supplier and a buyer, three rounds. Try to catch BATNA, framing, hedging and deadlock language. Three questions follow.
scenes.say_uz: Endi to‘liq muzokarani tinglang — yetkazib beruvchi va xaridor, uch raund. BATNA, framing, hedging va deadlock iboralarini tutib qolishga harakat qiling. Uch savol keladi.

scenes.title: Muzokara matni
board: Supplier: ballpark £52,000.
Buyer: in the region of £40,000.
Round 2: concessions both sides.
Round 3: deadlock → park & split the difference.
scenes.say_native: Tinglang. Ikkala tomonning anchorlarini va murosaga kelish jarayonini e’tibor bilan eshiting.
scenes.say: Supplier: We were thinking in the region of fifty-two thousand. Buyer: We'd need to be closer to forty. Supplier: That's below what we can do — but if you sign a two-year contract, we could go to forty-eight. Buyer: Forty-five, and you pay the freight. Supplier: Around forty-six, and we split the delivery cost. Buyer: Deal.
scenes.say_uz: Yetkazib beruvchi: biz qirq ikki ming atrofida o‘ylayapmiz. Xaridor: biz qirqqa yaqinroq bo‘lishimiz kerak. Yetkazib beruvchi: bu bizning imkoniyatimizdan past — ammo agar ikki yillik shartnomaga imzo chekayotgan bo‘lsangiz, qirq sakkizga tushishimiz mumkin. Xaridor: qirq besh va yuk tashishni siz to‘laysiz. Yetkazib beruvchi: qirq olti atrofida va yetkazish xarajatlarini o‘rtada bo‘lamiz. Xaridor: kelishdik.

scenes.title: Muzokara savollari
board: 1. What was the supplier's anchor?
2. What did the buyer trade?
3. How did they settle?
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Uch savolga javob bering: yetkazib beruvchining anchor raqami qanday edi? Xaridor nima berdi? Oqibatda qanday murosaga kelishdilar? Baland ovozda ingliz tilida javob bering.
scenes.say: Answer three questions aloud: What was the supplier's anchor? What did the buyer trade? And how did they finally settle?
scenes.say_uz: Uch savolga baland ovozda javob bering: yetkazib beruvchining anchor raqami qanday edi? Xaridor nima berdi? Oqibatda qanday kelishdilar?

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: Anchor: £52,000.
Buyer traded a two-year contract.
Settled at £46,000, freight shared.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar: anchor ellik ikki ming, xaridor ikki yillik shartnoma berdi, yakuniy narx qirq olti ming, yuk xarajati bo‘lingan. Ko‘rib turibsiz — muzokara bitta raqam emas, almashishlar seriyasi. Endi xatolarni ko‘ramiz.
scenes.say: Answers: the anchor was fifty-two thousand; the buyer traded a two-year contract; they settled on forty-six thousand with freight shared. A negotiation is never one number — it's a series of trades. Now the mistakes.
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar: anchor ellik ikki ming; xaridor ikki yillik shartnoma berdi; yakun qirq olti ming, yuk xarajati bo‘lingan. Muzokara bitta raqam emas — almashishlar seriyasi. Endi xatolarni ko‘ramiz.

scenes.title: Keng tarqalgan xato: birinchi taklifni har doim qabul qilish
board: ✗ Counterpart opens at £52,000 — you accept £52,000.
✓ Always counter with your anchor, even if reasonable.
Counter-anchor is not rude — it is the game.

examples.t: I hear you — we'd need to be closer to forty.
examples.uz: Fikringizni eshitdim — biz qirqqa yaqinroq bo‘lishimiz kerak.

scenes.say_native: Keng tarqalgan xato: birinchi taklifni darrov qabul qilish. Qarshi tomon ellik ikkidan boshladi — siz qabul qilasiz. Ingliz tilida “accepting the first offer” — bu muzokara emas, bu yon berish. Har doim o‘z anchoringizni qo‘ying, hatto birinchi taklif mantiqiy bo‘lsa ham: “I hear you — we'd need to be closer to forty.” Bu haqorat emas — bu o‘yinning qoidasi. Endi mashq qilamiz. Agar raqib birinchi raqam aytsa: “That’s higher than we can do — we were thinking around X.” — rad etmagan holda qarshi anchor.
scenes.say: A very common mistake: accepting the first offer. Your counterpart opens at fifty-two, and you say yes. In English this is called accepting the first offer — that's not negotiating, that's conceding. Always counter with your own anchor, even if theirs seems reasonable: “I hear you — we'd need to be closer to forty.” That's not rude; that's the game. Now practice.
scenes.say_uz: Keng tarqalgan xato: birinchi taklifni darrov qabul qilish. Raqib ellik ikkidan boshladi — siz ha deysiz. Bu muzokara emas, yon berish. Har doim o‘z anchoringizni qo‘ying, hatto mantiqiy bo‘lsa ham: “I hear you — we'd need to be closer to forty.” Bu haqorat emas — o‘yin qoidasi. Endi mashq.

scenes.title: Anchorga javob bering
board: Supplier opens at £52,000.
Counter with your anchor, aloud, politely
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Yetkazib beruvchi ellik ikkiga anchor qo‘ydi. Ovoz chiqarib muloyim qarshi anchor qo‘ying: “I hear you — we'd need to be closer to £42,000.” Sekin, samimiy va qat’iy ohangda ayting.
scenes.say: The supplier anchors at fifty-two thousand. Aloud — counter with your anchor, politely: “I hear you — we'd need to be closer to forty-two thousand.” Slow, warm and firm.
scenes.say_uz: Yetkazib beruvchi ellik ikki anchor qo‘ydi. Ovoz chiqarib muloyim qarshi anchor qo‘ying: “I hear you — we'd need to be closer to forty-two thousand.” Sekin, samimiy va qat’iy.

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: “I hear you — we'd need to be closer to £42,000.”
Then wait for their counter
scenes.say_native: Javoblar: “I hear you — we'd need to be closer to forty-two thousand.” va kutib turing — birinchi gapirmang. Endi yakuniy vazifani boshlaymiz.
scenes.say: Answers: “I hear you — we'd need to be closer to forty-two thousand,” then wait — don't speak first. Now the final task.
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar: “I hear you — we'd need to be closer to forty-two thousand.” Va kutib turing — birinchi gapirmang. Endi yakuniy vazifa.

scenes.title: Tinglash: maosh muzokarasi
board: Listen: employee and manager — salary review
Then two questions
scenes.say_native: Endi maosh muzokarasini tinglang — xodim va menejer o‘rtasida, yillik ko‘rib chiqishda. Anchor, hedging va concession iboralarini aniqlashga harakat qiling. Ikki savol tayyor — keyin javoblarni tekshiramiz.
scenes.say: Manager: We were thinking in the region of a six percent increase. Employee: I was hoping we could be a little more flexible — I brought in two major clients this year. Manager: That's true. If you stay through the December launch, we could go to nine. Employee: Around nine, and I'll also lead the next client pitch. Manager: Agreed — nine percent and the leadership role.
scenes.say_uz: Menejer: biz olti foiz atrofida o‘ylayapmiz. Xodim: biroz moslashuvchan bo‘lishingizni xohlardim — bu yil ikki yirik mijoz olib keldim. Menejer: rost. Agar dekabrdagi uchirilishigacha qolsangiz, to‘qquzga chiqishimiz mumkin. Xodim: to‘qqiz atrofida va keyingi mijoz taqdimotini men boshqaraman. Menejer: kelishdik — to‘qqiz foiz va yetakchilik roli.

scenes.title: Maosh muzokarasi savollari
board: 1. What was the manager's opening figure?
2. What did the employee trade for nine percent?
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Ikki savolga javob bering: menejerning birinchi raqami qanday edi? Xodim to‘qquz foiz evaziga nima berdi? Baland ovozda ingliz tilida javob bering.
scenes.say: Answer two questions aloud: What was the manager's opening figure? And what did the employee trade for nine percent?
scenes.say_uz: Ikki savolga baland ovozda javob bering: menejerning birinchi raqami qanday edi? Xodim to‘qquz foiz evaziga nima berdi?

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: Manager anchored at 6%.
Employee traded staying through the launch + leading the next pitch.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar: menejer olti foizdan ochdi; xodim dekabr uchishigacha qolish va keyingi mijoz taqdimotini boshqarishga va’da berib to‘qquz foizga erishdi. Almashish — xuddi oldingi raundlardagi kabi ishlaydi. Endi yakuniy vazifaga o‘tamiz.
scenes.say: Answers: the manager anchored at six percent; the employee traded staying through the December launch and leading the next client pitch for nine percent. Trading works the same here as in every round. Now the final task.
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar: menejer olti foiz anchor qo‘ydi; xodim dekabr uchirilishigacha qolib va keyingi mijoz taqdimotini boshqarib to‘qquz foizga erishdi. Almashish har raundda bir xil ishlaydi. Endi yakuniy vazifa.

scenes.title: 60 soniya: o‘z pozitsiyangiz
board: Record 60 seconds: state your anchor, one trade, one BATNA line
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Olmiy kunlik xo‘jayiningiz yoki mijozingizga qarata oltmish soniya gaplang: anchoringiz, bitta almashuv va BATNA chizig‘ingiz bo‘lsin. Telefoningizga yozib oling va baland ovozda eshiting.
scenes.say: Record sixty seconds aimed at a boss or a client: your anchor, one trade, and one BATNA line. Speak slowly and clearly, and listen back afterwards.
scenes.say_uz: Oltmish soniya xo‘jayiningiz yoki mijozingizga qaratib gapiring: anchoringiz, bitta almashuv va BATNA chizig‘ingiz bo‘lsin. Sekin va tiniq gapiring, keyin yozuvni eshiting.

scenes.title: Yakuniy vazifa: uch raundli muzokara skripti
board: Write a 3-round script: anchors → trades → deadlock break
Include BATNA line and one concession exchange
scenes.say_native: Yakuniy vazifa: uch raundli muzokara ssenariysi yozing. Birinchi raundda anchorlar, ikkinchi raundda almashishlar, uchinchi raundda deadlock yechimi bo‘lsin. BATNA chizig‘ini va kamida bitta concession almashuvini kiriting. Ovoz chiqarib o‘qing. Ssenariy yozishda real odamni tasavvur qiling: kimdir muhandis, kimdir moliyachi — ularning tillari ham boshqacha, muzokarada shu farqni his qilish kerak.
scenes.say: Final task: write a three-round negotiation script. Round one — anchors; round two — trades; round three — breaking the deadlock. Include a BATNA line and at least one concession exchange. Read it aloud when done.
scenes.say_uz: Yakuniy vazifa: uch raundli muzokara ssenariysi yozing. Birinchi raund — anchorlar; ikkinchi raund — almashishlar; uchinchi raund — deadlock yechimi. BATNA chizig‘ini va kamida bitta concession almashuvini kiriting. Tayyor bo‘lgach, baland ovozda o‘qing.

scenes.title: Bugun nimani o‘rgandik
board: BATNA · Anchoring · Framing
Hedging · Concession trading
Deadlock: park it · split it
scenes.say_native: Xulosa. Tayyorgarlik va BATNA tilini, anchoring va framing texnikalarini, hedging va yumshatish iboralarini, concession almashuvini, deadlock yechish iboralarini va birinchi taklifni qabul qilmaslik qoidasini o‘rgandik. Keyingi darsda biznes yozishmalari — rasmiy emaillar va taklif xatlari. Bu ko‘nikmalar sizga nafaqat biznesda, balki ish joyidagi har qanday kelishuvda — ta’til, loyiha muddati, jamoa vazifalarida — yordam beradi.
scenes.say: Recap: preparation and BATNA language, anchoring and framing, hedging and softening, trading concessions, deadlock tactics, and never accepting the first offer. Next time: business writing — formal emails and proposal letters.
scenes.say_uz: Xulosa: tayyorgarlik va BATNA tili; anchoring va framing; hedging; concession almashuvi; deadlock taktikalari; birinchi taklifni qabul qilmaylik. Keyingi darsda biznes yozishmalari.

scenes.title: Uy vazifasi va keyingi dars
board: Homework: write a negotiation script with 3 rounds
Check: anchors · one trade · one deadlock phrase · BATNA line
Next lesson: P2-02 business correspondence
scenes.say_native: Uy vazifasi: uch raundli muzokara ssenariysi — anchorlar, almashish, deadlock — BATNA chizig‘i va bir concession almashuvi bilan. Mezon: har raunda kamida bitta hedging iborasi, oxirida ikkala tomon podpis beradigan yakuniy taklif bo‘lsin. Keyingi darsda biznes yozishmalari. Uy vazifasini yozgach, o‘zingizga ovoz chiqarib o‘qib bering — monologingiz ravon bo‘lsa, muzokarada ham ravon bo‘ladi.
scenes.say: Homework: write a negotiation script with three rounds — anchors, a trade and a deadlock break — with a BATNA line and at least one concession exchange. Success criteria: at least one hedging phrase per round, and a final offer both sides can sign. Next time: business correspondence.
scenes.say_uz: Uy vazifasi: uch raundli muzokara ssenariysi — anchorlar, almashish va deadlock — BATNA chizig‘i va concession almashuvi bilan. Mezon: har raunda kamida bitta hedging iborasi va imzolash mumkin bo‘lgan yakuniy taklif. Keyingi darsda biznes yozishmalari.

homework_uz: Uy vazifasi: uch raundli muzokara ssenariysi yozing — anchorlar, almashish va deadlock yechimi — BATNA chizig‘i va kamida bitta concession almashuvi bilan.
